candidates.review_note: The probability of a complete draw-color sequence in a Polya urn is a product of rising per-color factors divided by the common total rising product, hence invariant under permutations of draw positions. By exchangeability and consistency under marginalization, a specified subsequence of n draw positions has the same joint law as the first n draws. Multiply the n requested color probabilities with only previously requested colors reinforced; the actual gaps x_i do not enter. Compute numerator and denominator as exact integers and reduce once by their gcd. This is not treating reinforcement as independent draws; the count of previous requested occurrences is retained.

Resolve every fixed arrow chain to an undecided cell or the outside sink. Any cycle consisting only of fixed arrows invalidates the entire grid because every starting cell must escape. Each undecided cell then has four labeled choices of destination in the compressed graph; choices returning to itself are invalid. A valid replacement is exactly a directed spanning tree oriented toward the outside sink, with parallel choices counted separately. Construct the outgoing Laplacian minor and use the directed matrix-tree theorem; its determinant modulo the prime counts all valid choices. Modular Gaussian elimination handles row swaps and zero pivots, and an empty determinant is one when all fixed chains escape.
